why: phở has the dipping tone: phố (rising tone) means street.
được không? at the end asks whether your price is OK.
bao nhiêu tiền asks about money; bao nhiêu tuổi asks about age.
Prices count thousands: hai trăm nghìn.
rẻ has no vowel mark on the e: rể is a son-in-law, rễ a root.

hint: quần · màu đen · the color comes last

why: Use chị for a woman a little older; có … không asks do you have.
trái is left; phải is right.
có … không around xa: Có xa không?

q: Hồ Gươm cách đây bao xa? asks…
o: how far Hoan Kiem Lake is from here
how long it takes on foot

q: On a motorbike taxi, Take me to the airport =
why: Cho tôi đến + place: take me to.
phải has the dipping tone; phái (rising tone) is a different word.
này comes after the noun: khách sạn này.

why: bao xa stays at the end, where the answer goes.

p: How far is the market from here?
why: bao xa asks how far.

phải has the dipping tone: right.

why: Use chị for a woman a little older, and em for yourself.

rưỡi comes after giờ.

q: Hôm nay là ngày bao nhiêu? asks…
why: ngày bao nhiêu asks the date; thứ mấy asks the day of the week.

p: What time do you go to work? (to a man a little older)
why: Use anh for a man a little older; mấy giờ asks the time.

q: Tại sao anh không đi làm? The best answer is…
why: Answer tại sao with vì: because.
nên introduces the result: so.
bị + the problem: bị đau đầu.
vì gives the reason, nên gives the result.
lạc means lost, and bị marks something bad that happened.
ốm has the rising tone: ôm (level tone) means hug.

why: mưa has a vowel mark (the horn): mua means buy.
bị goes before something bad that happens to you; no là.

p: Because it's raining, I'm staying home.
why: After a vì part, the result starts with nên.
bị goes before something bad that happens to you.

p: Why didn't you come? (to a woman a little older)
why: tại has the heavy tone: tại sao means why.
ốm has the rising tone: ôm (level tone) means hug.

p: It's raining, so I'm staying home
why: mưa has a vowel mark (the horn): mua means buy.

p: Do you have a headache? (to an old man)
why: Use ông for an old man, and wrap the question in có … không.

q: Could I have a glass of water, please? (to someone a little older) =
why: Cho em xin + what you want, and ạ at the end.
mời invites: the speaker is offering.

q: Which word softens a friendly suggestion, like OK? at the end?
why: nhé softens; ạ shows respect.

q: Your teacher calls your name. You answer…
why: Dạ is the polite answer when someone older calls you; ừ is only for friends and younger people.

q: Excuse me, can I ask you something? (to a woman a little older) =
why: Call her chị, call yourself em, and ask with cho em hỏi.

why: cà has the falling tone mark: cà phê.

p: Two iced teas, please (to a stall-holder a little older)
why: Drinks are counted by the glass: the classifier cốc goes before the noun.

p: Please have a seat (to a woman your parents' age)
why: mời invites, and cô fits a woman your parents' age.

p: Please have a seat. (to a man)
why: mời invites someone to do something.

p: Wait for me a moment, OK? (to a woman a little older)
why: nhé at the end softens a request.

p: Thank you. (polite, to an older woman)
why: ạ, with the dot below, shows respect; à asks a surprised question.

p: Two iced teas, please (politely, to a stall-holder a little older)

why: trà has the falling tone mark.

p: One bowl of beef pho, please (politely, to a stall-holder a little older)
hint: cho · em · một · bát · phở bò · ạ
why: bát is the classifier for a bowl, and bò comes after the noun: phở bò.

p: Excuse me, can I ask something? (to a man a little older)
why: Call him anh and yourself em: Anh ơi, cho em hỏi.
